note: Every rule that lives at the WRITER's boundary, in one document. This tier exists because no other tier reaches them: accept and format both RE-RENDER, and a re-render applies neither rounding nor shortening, so until this directory existed the whole of SPEC 4.5.4 was beyond the corpus and each implementation carried its own tests for it. BOTH ELEVATION TIES ARE LOAD-BEARING AND NEITHER IS DECORATIVE. Measured against the five wrong tie rules an implementation actually reaches for, each catches a different half and only the PAIR identifies round-half-to-even. 340.25 is 340.2 under the rule and 340.3 under half-away-from-zero and half-up-toward-positive-infinity, so it catches those two - and half-up is what the scaled trick Math.round(x*10)/10 does in both JavaScript and Java. 340.75 is 340.8 under the rule and 340.7 under half-toward-zero and half-down-toward-negative-infinity, so it catches the other two. Half-to-odd is caught by either. A fixture carrying only one of them looks like tie coverage and leaves two wrong rules passing. NEGATIVE TIES ARE NOT NEEDED HERE and their absence is deliberate rather than an oversight: every one of those five rules is already caught by one of the two positive values, so -340.25 would add a value and no discrimination. Do not drop either number for looking redundant beside the other; they are not. THIS PARAGRAPH REPLACES ONE THAT SAID 340.75 'DECIDES NOTHING' - written here, in the note warning against deleting the awkward-looking value, by the person who put both values in. The measurement above was made afterwards, because somebody re-checked a claim that had already been published. Treat a sentence in a fixture note that calls part of the fixture decorative as unmeasured until you have the table. THE FIFTH CHANNEL IS DELIBERATE: SPEC 4.5.4 rounds longitude and latitude to 6 places and elevation to 1, and rounding is only definable where the units are known, so a channel this version does not name is written back unchanged - 0.98765432 survives verbatim while the elevation beside it rounds to 512.5. The negative zeros are ones the WRITER CREATES rather than ones it was handed: -0.00000004 and -0.04 carry no negative zero into the writer and would carry one out of it in most languages, and format/ can only ever supply -0.0 as an input literal. `hidden: false` must not be written; the declared version 0.1.99 must be written back rather than the reader's own; the interior null at pip 3 must not be shortened away, because dropping it would move the time into the elevation channel.
